channel.title: brokenXoxo — Blog
channel.description: Notes on building things: WhatsApp bots, AI agents, scrapers, and the unglamorous parts.

item.title: Tirana has fought five days straight, and Albania's students say they are done waiting
item.description: Petrol bombs and cobblestones against water cannon and tear gas, with rubber bullets reportedly used for the first time. 80 charged, hundreds arrested, and Rama blames foreign actors.

item.title: Apple's first foldable sold out of its launch window in a weekend
item.description: Preorders for the iPhone Duo opened Friday. US delivery estimates now run to January 2027, and Apple calls early demand "nothing short of extraordinary".

item.title: An Irish priest killed at Passchendaele while going to help wounded men is a step closer to sainthood
item.description: Fr Willie Doyle was killed at Passchendaele going to the aid of two wounded Protestant soldiers. On Sunday, 3,500 pages of evidence go to Rome.

item.title: A fire at Canada's main live-fire training base has killed and injured people, and nobody will say how many
item.description: Defence Minister David McGuinty confirmed deaths and injuries at CFB Wainwright in Alberta but gave no numbers, calling the situation "very, very active and delicate".

item.title: US overdose deaths are falling, and the drugs killing people are getting harder to reverse
item.description: Fentanyl cut with animal tranquillisers is spreading, and naloxone does not work on them. In one Ohio county, 78% of fatal overdoses last year involved stimulants.

item.title: Satellite images show Kim Jong Un's summer fleet, including an 80m yacht with a 50m pool
item.description: The BBC tracked four large vessels around Wonsan from July to October. Most North Koreans are legally entitled to 14 days leave a year, and rarely get to take it.

item.title: France's student protests turned into a night of arson and looting, and the arrest toll passed 1,000
item.description: An estimated 550,000 marched over school conditions and the cost of living. Town halls burned in Limoges and Lyon, an Apple store was emptied in Lille, and 60 officers were injured.

item.title: Masked settlers attacked a European diplomatic convoy in the West Bank, and Israel's own offices disagree on what happened
item.description: Belgium, France, Poland and the Catholic Church sent envoys to Taybeh to assess settler attacks on the olive harvest. A consul's car was smashed and a French mayor was beaten.

item.title: Trump waived the Russia sanctions two days before they took effect, and his own party objected
item.description: The law he signed in September gave him power to tariff buyers of Russian oil and sanction Putin himself. On Friday night he suspended most of it, citing national interest.

item.title: The Galaxy Tab S9 just got its last big Android update, and the A9 series is already done
item.description: One UI 9 is the final major OS upgrade for the Tab S9 line. The cheaper Tab A9, launched the same year, already had its last one, because it shipped under the old policy.

item.title: OpenAI is building a humanoid robot, and Altman says the body is the easy part
item.description: Sam Altman told the Sources podcast "we will" build a humanoid, with a demo expected in 2027. His focus is the brain, not the body, and 27 robotics roles are open.

item.title: TikTok permanently banned the ad account for Alex Gibney's Musk documentary
item.description: Bleecker Street was told the account had been permanently suspended over its political content. TikTok and X are the only two platforms still refusing to run ads for the film.

item.title: Anthropic says it is hiring fewer juniors, and everyone is in more meetings
item.description: Anthropic's own workplace report says junior technical staff fell from 21% to 14%, junior technical hires from 27% to 9%, and meeting time is up 20% in a year.

item.title: Meta quietly dropped the terms line that looked like a licence to scrape every publisher's site
item.description: Meta's updated commercial terms said it could use content from a business account's domains, web pages and URLs to train its models. After lawyers and reporters noticed, the provision is gone.

item.title: Meta is running a $1M hackathon, and applications close on October 25
item.description: Ten days, $1,000,000 in prizes, two tracks and a hard cap of 20,000 applicants reviewed on a rolling basis. Applying early is the whole strategy.
